key_takeaways: US documents for Italy count for only six months from the date of issue and the Atto Notorio for about 90 days, so order and apostille birth certificates four to six months out and swear the Atto Notorio last.

The US does not issue a Nulla Osta certificate: each of you swears a Dichiarazione Giurata at the US post for your wedding region (USD 50 per notary seal), then has it legalized at a Prefettura, generally in the same consular district, with a EUR 16 revenue stamp.

The Italian consulates in New York and Los Angeles ask for four Atto Notorio witnesses who are not related to you, while the US Embassy says two, so confirm the number with your consulate before you ask anyone.

A marriage valid in Italy is automatically valid in the US, and the US Embassy describes no US registration step: apostille the Italian certificate at the Prefettura before you fly home, then update Social Security first, followed by your passport and driver's license.

Official stamps and consular fees are modest, but town hall hire runs from EUR 500 to EUR 9,200 (about USD 576 to USD 10,595 at the Italian consular rate for October to December 2026), and extra nights in the consulate city are where budgets slip.

faq.q: Do Americans need a Nulla Osta to marry in Italy?
faq.a: Not as a certificate, which the US does not issue. Each American partner swears a Dichiarazione Giurata in Italy instead, which Italian offices accept as the Nulla Osta.

faq.q: How many days before the wedding do we need to be in Italy?
faq.a: No official source sets a minimum number of days. Procedures can take several days, per the US Embassy, and your comune's banns period decides the rest.

faq.q: Can our parents or siblings be our witnesses?
faq.a: At the ceremony, the Embassy's rules do not exclude relatives; confirm with your comune. For the Atto Notorio, the US Embassy says no: those witnesses cannot be family or in-laws; check your consulate.

faq.q: Is a marriage in Italy legally recognized in the US?
faq.a: Yes, automatically, if it is valid in Italy. The US Embassy describes no step to register the marriage in the US: your apostilled Italian certificate is the proof.

faq.q: Can a same-sex couple from the US marry in Italy?
faq.a: Italian law offers same-sex couples civil unions, not marriage (Law 76/2016). Ask your comune or a lawyer licensed in Italy how this applies to two foreign nationals, and see our guide for same-sex couples.
